page.layout: One column of running text. Above it: running head at top left, page number at top right. Centred below them: the sermon heading "CONCIO VI", then the scripture reference "Genef. 20." set apart. Body is one text block with a decorated initial. No marginal notes. Signature "E" at the foot.

p.i: Tprofectus est inde (ex Ma-bre) Abraham in terram australem, habitauitq; inter Cades, & inter Sur, & peregrinatus est in Gerar. Dixitq; Abraham de Sara uxore sua: Soror mea est: & misit Abimelech rex Gerar, & tulit Saram. Venit autem Deus ad Abimelech in somnio noctis, & dixit ad eum: Ecce tu morieris propter mulierem quam accepisti, est enim marito iuncta. Abimelech vero non accesserat ad eam: & ait: Domine, num quid interficies quoque gentem iustam? An non ipse dixit mihi, soror mea est? cum integritate cordis mei, & cum innocentia manuum mearum feci hoc. Dixitq; ad eum Deus per somnium: Etiam ego novi, quòd in integritate cordis tui feceris hoc, & prohibui etiam ego te, ne peccares in me, atque ideo non permisi ut tangeres eam. Nunc igitur restitue uxorem viro, est enim propheta, & orabit pro te, ut vivas: quòd si non restitueris, scito quòd moriendo morieris et

page.notes: Small reference signs (a stroke-and-circle mark, printed before "Abraham" and "Abimelech") are not transcribed; they are printing marks, not words. The large initial "T" is decorative and joined to "profectus" as the rule for woodcut initials requires. Long s and s read as plain s throughout. The line "Saram. Venit" and "Dixitq;" are as printed. Continues on the next page mid-sentence ("et").
